newsitem.title: USA: Further US income gains, low inflation - Stiglitz.
newsitem.headline: Further US income gains, low inflation - Stiglitz.

text.p: White House economic adviser Joseph Stiglitz said economic data indicated there would be more gains in personal income and low inflation in the future.

Stiglitz told reporters at the White House that in the third quarter of 1996, the private sector grew at a 3 percent annual rate, and equipment investment rose at an "astonishing" 19 percent annual rate. Real disposable income rose by 4.9 percent and inflation remained very subdued, he said.
"Such strong private sector growth and investment bodes well for further income gains and low inflation in the future," Stiglitz said.

Stiglitz is the head of the president's Council of Economic Advisers. He spoke after the government reported that the nation's gross domestic product expanded at a 2.2 percent annual rate in the three months from July through September, less than half the booming 4.7 percent pace posted during the second quarter.
Laura Tyson, chair of Clinton's National Economic Council, said consumer confidence is at the highest level in six years.
"We anticipate that based on the income growth numbers and the consumer confidence numbers that consumer spending will remain strong," she told reporters.
Stiglitz agreed, saying that despite the relatively weak consumer spending in the third quarter, "there are very strong reasons to believe that there will be a pickup in consumer spending."

He said net exports "were not as strong as one would have liked" in the third quarter, but that was largely because the United States had been growing faster than its trading partners and this had made America import more. Now, he said, "there is some growth in some of the European countries that looks like it's going to pick up and that will strengthen that part of the GDP as well."
Stiglitz indicated he was not alarmed by a rising backlog of inventories in the third quarter.

"The fact is that the inventory/sales ratios remain lean. They were very lean in the second quarter and now there has been some restocking but the inventory relative to the sales are still at a very moderate level."
